deviations: UGX to USD conversion uses a fixed 3700 UGX/USD; the paper does not state the rate (control means of price, harvest value and expenses match the paper's within about 1%).
Table 6 col 8: own/family hours were not collected at baseline, so the ANCOVA control for profit incl. own hours is the household's baseline monetary profit.
Family hours are valued at one market wage: the median daily hired-labour wage (5000 UGX) divided by the median hours per day (6), i.e. 833 UGX/hour, not a community-specific wage.
Table 2 cols 4-5: the enumerator-measured bag weights (y) are matched to sales by bag order after dropping the randomly selected lab bag; the authors' exact matching is unknown.

Post-harvest hired labour in seasons 5-7 is the sum of the activity items (decob/winnow/sort/bag), not the survey total labor_cost_ph. This drops one 12m UGX entry that appears only in the total. It was chosen because the expenses R2 (0.33) and the profit R2 (0.22) then match the paper.
notes: Table 2: every quantity comes from anonym_returns_data.dta. Visual defects are the sum of ten indicators (insects = live or dead) over the 622 bags with any defect recorded, with village FE and household-clustered SEs. Lab defects are the share of the 200 g sample, with village FE and robust SEs. Sales are add5 rosters 2-4; roster 1 is the single lab bag bought by the team. That gives 116 sales from 94 households, with village and week-of-sale FE and household clusters. Control means match the paper (2.46, 0.32, 731.25, 3.73, 704.5), and so do the SEs for cols 3 and 5. Table 6 Panel A uses panel_g1 (follow-up seasons 4-7) and seller_data (prices). Each outcome is regressed on treatment, season dummies and the household's most recent baseline value of the outcome, with village-clustered SEs. Households with no baseline value are dropped, which gives N=617 for price. Harvest value is harvest times the household's average sale price, or the community-season average price if it did not sell. Expenses are inputs, hired labour, post-harvest labour and other costs, drying/storage and transport. I chose the pre-value definition (most recent baseline, not the baseline mean) and the harvest value and expense definitions by matching the paper's non-claimed Table 6 entries (N, R2, the acreage/harvest/expenses coefficients and control means), after one claim comparison (attempt-5). The final run reproduces every Table 6 N and R2. Remaining gaps: yield 113.6 vs 108.9; Table 2 deductions 0.14 vs 0.18 and net price 1.58 vs 0.98 (bag-to-sale matching). Attempts 1-4, 6 and 7 are exploratory runs with no RESULT lines; attempts 6-7 print only non-claimed coefficients, N and R2. No run hung; each sandbox run took about 1-3 s. README.pdf and 'other/Results reported in the main text.pdf' in the mount were read as documentation.
